sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the relinquishment of the subject properties in favour of the BDA touches the business of the Co-operative Society, and suit having been filed without issuing notice to the Registrar concerned as specified under Section 125 of the Act is not maintainable.

In support, he places reliance on the decision of the full bench of this Court in the case of the Krishi Mattu Ksheera Utpadaka Vividoodesha Sahakari Sangh Niyamit Bakkal and another Vs. Sohan Lal reported in AIR 1993 KAR 20.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent-plaintiffs submits that the relinquishment of the properties in favour of the first defendant BDA does not touch the business of the Co-operative Society, and the subject properties were relinquished in terms of Section 32 of BDA.
Hence, he submits that the impugned order passed by the Trial Court is in accordance with law, and the same does not warrant interference.

In support he places reliance on the decision of the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Vinayaka Graha Nirmana Sahakara Sangha ltd. Vs.
Karnataka Appellate Tribunal and others reported in 1995 6 KLJ 573.

sentences.text: I have examined the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.

6. The Plaintiff among other reliefs has sought for declaration to declare that the deed executed by the second defendant-Co-operative Society in favour of the first defendant relinquishing the subject properties is not binding on the plaintiff.

7. Section 125 of the Act specifies that, no suit shall be instituted against the Co-operative Society or any of its officers in respect of any act touching the constitution, management or the business of the society until the expiration of two months next after notice in writing has been delivered to the Registrar.
To put it simply, no suit can be registered against the cooperative society without issuing notice to the Registrar concerned.
The second defendant is in the business of acquiring land and forming layouts and allotting plots to its members.

In the instant case, the second defendant after forming the layout and in terms of the sanctioned layout plan has relinquished the civic amenity site and open space which are the subject - 10 - properties, in favour of the first defendant and relinquishment of the said sites touches the business of the society.

8. The full bench of this Court in the case of Krishi Mattu Ksheera Utpadaka Vividoodesha Sahakari Sangh Niyamit Bakkal and another (Supra) at page No.93 has held as follows:
In the light of the foregoing dictum of the Supreme Court there can possibly be no doubt at all that the expression 'any act' appearing in Sec. 125 is referable not merely to an illegal omission but also to an omission simpliciter.

In the circumstance it behoves on our part to fall in step with the views of the apex Court as aforesaid and in M/S Poornaprajna House Building Co ... vs Smt. Bylamma on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16513363/
7 the light of the same to hold that the expression 'any act' referred to in Sec.125 is not confined to illegal omissions alone but also covers a mere omission simpliciter.

entities.text: M/S Poornaprajna House Building Co ... vs Smt. Bylamma on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text:
In fine our answers to the questions formulated are:
(1) (i) Notice under Section 125 is mandatory, where the act in question is with reference to the society.

Such notice is also necessary if the 'act' in question is with reference to an officer of the society and the 'act' or omission complained of relates to the Constitution, management or business of the society.
(ii) Notice is also mandatory where the 'act' in question covers both the society and the officer.

(2) The expression 'any act' referred to in Sec. 125 of the Act is not confined to illegal omissions alone but also covers a mere omission simpliciter.
9.

In view of the ratio enunciated by the full bench of this court supra, I am of the view that the plaintiff before - 11 - challenging the action of the society in relinquishing the subject properties in favour of the first defendant was required to issue notice to the Registrar as mandated under Section 125 of the Act.

The decision relied upon by the learned counsel for the respondent in the case of Vinayaka Graha Nirmana Sahakara Sangha ltd (supra) is not applicable to the facts of the case, since the plaintiff therein had sought for declaration to declare that he is the owner of the property therein, and had complained about the interference of the Co-operative Society in respect of the property therein.

The second defendant had also filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 (d)
stating that the plaint averment clearly discloses that the subject properties have been acquired by the Government under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act 1894.
Hence, the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to declare the plaintiff as owner of the subject properties in respect of the land which has been acquired under the provisions of the land acquisition.

2. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Y.P. Sudhanva Reddy and others Vs.
Chairman and Managing - 13 - Director Karnataka Milk Federation and others at para-19 to 21 has held as follows:
19.

Chairman and Managing - 13 - Director Karnataka Milk Federation and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In other words, on and after issuance of the notifications under the Act and initiation of acquisition proceedings by the State which culminated in passing of the award as far back as in the year 1941, the appellants' predecessor-in-title ceased to be the owner of the suit land and lost all his rights to hold the suit land and claim possession over it.

20. The only legal remedy available to the appellants' predecessor-in-title (Mr K.G.
Yellappa Reddy) in such case was to challenge the legality and correctness of the notifications issued under Section 4 or/and 6 of the Act and that too within a reasonable time after their issuance in the year 1941.

It is not in dispute that the landowners, admittedly, did not challenge the validity and correctness of the notifications and, on the other hand, by suppressing the fact of acquisition proceedings from the Court filed two suits one after the other and claimed title over the suit land.

21. In our considered opinion, neither the predecessor-in- title of the appellants and nor the appellants had any subsisting right, title and interest in the suit land on and after 1941 consequent upon issuance of the notifications by the State under the Act.
The reason was that all the ownership rights of the appellants' predecessor-in-title in the suit land stood vested in the State once the acquisition proceedings were completed under the Act.

As mentioned above, the appellants' only right was to either challenge the land acquisition proceedings as being against the provisions of the Act or to claim compensation payable under the Act in relation to the suit land under Section 11 of the Act followed by reference proceedings under Section 18 of the Act M/S Poornaprajna House Building Co ... vs Smt. 4. In the absence of challenge to the said acquisition proceedings, the plaintiff having no subsisting right/title over the suit property cannot maintain the suit for declaration.

ORDER i) Petition is allowed.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The second defendant is in the business of acquiring land and forming layouts and allotting plots to its members.
In the instant case, the second defendant after forming the layout and in terms of the sanctioned layout plan has relinquished the civic amenity site and open space which are the subject - 10 - properties, in favour of the first defendant and relinquishment of the said sites touches the business of the society.

21. In our considered opinion, neither the predecessor-in- title of the appellants and nor the appellants had any subsisting right, title and interest in the suit land on and after 1941 consequent upon issuance of the notifications by the State under the Act.
The plaint averment discloses that the suit property having being acquired by the government under the provisions of Land acquisition Act, the plaintiff is having no subsisting right/title in the suit property, since suit property vested with the government free from all encumbrances.
opennyai_summary.decision: 4. In the absence of challenge to the said acquisition proceedings, the plaintiff having no subsisting right/title over the suit property cannot maintain the suit for declaration.
